ALBANY, NEW YORK

May 8, 1995

3:04 p.m.

REGULAR SESSION SENATOR JOHN A. DeFRANCISCO, Acting President STEPHEN F. SLOAN, Secretary

P R O C E E D I N G S

The Senate will come to order. Would everyone please rise and repeat with me the Pledge of Allegiance.

The invocation today will be given by Imam Abdur Rahim Muhammad, the Chaplain and Islamic Services Coordinator of the Elmira Correctional Facility.

Dear members of the Senate and all those present, peace be upon you. Inshallah 'alaihim, salam alaihum!

Please allow me to express my gratitude to Senator Kuhl and those who have made this historic occasion possible. I thank Almighty God and am once honored and humbled to represent the Nation of Islam and the hundreds of thousands of Muslims everywhere across New York State. As probably the first and more probably not the last Muslim to open in prayer before this honorable gathering, let me make but one request, that each of us look to our own beliefs, values, disciplines and principles to find instead of that in which we could angrily disagree, those great many things on which, with united hearts and minds, we can and should act together to build a better reality for everyone under the blessings of the one God of us all.

I am blessed to be able to work with men in prison every day and just recently returned from Kazakhstan, a country where entire people was freed from mental and spiritual incarceration. In prayer, let us see the challenge of responding to freedom by respecting it.

Islam is a religion that has been represented and also misrepresented. In repre senting it here, I reflect on the words of Imam W. D. Muhammad who once said it's not who we are; it's what we represent that is important. This religion of peace is nowhere better repre sented than in the opening seven verses of the Qur'an, in which I pray that those honored lawmakers here will find its echo in their own minds and hearts with deeds, words and translation, we pray.

A'udhu billahi minash shaitanir rajim.

I seek refuge in the forces of Almighty God from all evil.

Bismillahir rahmanir rahim.

The merciful benefactor of the merciful redeemer.

Al hamdu lil lahi rabbil alamin.

Praise be to Allah, the cherisher and sustainer of the word.

Arrahmanir rahim.

The merciful benefactor, the merciful redeemer.

Maliki Yawmuddin.

Master of the day of judgment.

Iyyaka na'budu wa iyyaka nasta'in.

You do we worship and Your help do we seek.

Ihdinas siratal mustaqim. Show us the straight way.

Siratal ladhina 'amta 'alaihim, ghairil maghdubi 'alaihim wa lad dallin.

The way of those on whom You have bestowed Your grace, those whose portion is not ra, and who go not astray. Amin, amin. Amen.

Reading of the journal.

In Senate, Sunday, May 7th. The Senate met pursuant to adjournment, Senator Hoblock in the Chair. The Journal of Saturday, May 6th, was read and approved. On motion, Senate adjourned.

Without objection, the Journal stands approved as read.

Presentation of petitions.

Messages from the Assembly.

Messages from the Governor.

Secretary will read.

The Governor returns without executive approval Senate Bill Number 1294, entitled An act to amend the Estates, Powers and Trusts Law, in relation to the exercise of powers of appointment; by Senator Lack, Veto Message Number 5.

Also the Governor returned without executive approval Senate Bill Number 2134, an act to amend the Estates, Powers and Trusts Law, in relation to a share of stock; by Senator Lack, Veto Number 8.

Reports of standing committees.

Reports of select committees.

Communications and reports from state officers.

Motions and resolutions.

Senator Tully.

Yes, Mr. President. On behalf of Senator Lack, on page 44, I offer the following amendments to Calendar Number 115, Senate Print Number 985-A, and ask that said bill retain its place on the Third Reading Calendar.

Amendments received.

Mr. President, on behalf of Senator Cook, on page 47, I offer the following amendments to Calendar Number 495, Senate Print Number 3156, and ask that said bill retain its place on the Third Reading Calendar.

Amendments received.
